newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico to repay U.S., IMF loans early.
newsitem.headline: Mexico to repay U.S., IMF loans early.

text.p: Mexico will repay immediately the outstanding $3.5 billion of an emergency loan from the U.S. Treasury and will also repay early $1.5 billion to the International Monetary Fund (IMF), Finance Minister Guillermo Ortiz said Wednesday.
Speaking live on television from a ceremony at the presidential palace, Ortiz said he had received instructions from President Ernesto Zedillo to make the payments tomorrow.

Mexico had borrowed $12.5 billion from the U.S. Treasury to shore up its economy in the wake of the disastrous December 1994 peso devaluation but had already repaid $9 billion of that prior to Thursday's announcement. The borrowed money was backed by Mexican oil revenues.
Mexico also borrowed heavily from the International Monetary Fund (IMF). After Thursday's repayment, it will still have billions of dollars outstanding to the IMF.

Ortiz said the early repayments -- financed by borrowing on international markets -- would save $100 million in interest payments, eliminate uncertainty and put the Mexican economy in a more solid position.
